ui.tagline: 100% free daily tarot reading. Pick your own cards from the deck. No signup, no cost, ever.
ui.heroTitleLine1: What do today's cards reveal about
ui.funFact: Fun fact: The vintage look of our tarot cards is authentic. We use the traditional 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith Tarot with the original artwork by Pamela Colman Smith. More than a century later, this classic deck continues to inspire readers around the world and is considered one of the most influential foundations of modern tarot.

determinant.label: The Determinant
determinant.subtitle: The force shaping the whole day
intros: Setting the tone for the whole day:
Before anything else, shaping the day:

present.label: The Present
present.subtitle: Where you actually stand
intros: Right now, at the center of things:
What you're dealing with right now:

future.label: The Future
future.subtitle: Where this is heading
intros: Just ahead, this is moving toward:
Where this is heading, if nothing changes:
The near future is pointing toward:

summaryClauses: {determinant} anchors today's reading. {past} and {future} complete the arc.
{determinant} sets the tone for today. {past} shaped where you've been; {future} shows where you're headed.

0.name: The Fool
0.upright: a fresh start with no map and no guarantees — nothing to go on but curiosity and the nerve to step forward before every answer is in.
0.reversed: hesitation dressed up as prudence, a step rehearsed so many times it never gets taken — or the opposite: a leap made blind, without checking what's underneath.
0.advice: Be a beginner again. The only mistake here is refusing to start.

1.name: The Magician
1.upright: realizing every tool the situation calls for — intellect, skill, timing — is already in your hands, and using them on purpose is the only step left.
1.reversed: talent sitting unused, or skill bent toward manipulation instead of building something. Either way, ability is going to waste, or confidence is more performance than foundation.
1.advice: Stop collecting more tools. Pick up the one in your hand and use it.

2.name: The High Priestess
2.upright: knowledge that comes in under language — a hunch, a dream, a feeling that ends up more accurate than any evidence you had at the time.
2.reversed: a quiet truth getting drowned out by noise, or an instinct kept private because it can't yet prove itself.
2.advice: Trust what you already sense but haven't said out loud. It knows something your reasoning hasn't caught up to yet.

3.name: The Empress
3.upright: a season of growth that wants tending, not forcing — a project, relationship, or part of yourself that thrives once it's fed instead of pushed.
3.reversed: care or creativity tipping into smothering, or fertile ground left untended until it stopped producing anything.
3.advice: Give what you care about attention instead of pressure. Patience is what grows it.

4.name: The Emperor
4.upright: order built on purpose — a framework, boundary, or plan sturdy enough to hold good intentions up under real pressure.
4.reversed: control gripped too tightly, or a structure so loose nothing inside it stays upright.
4.advice: Put up the scaffolding before you build the house. Structure now saves effort later.

5.name: The Hierophant
5.upright: wisdom handed down through established channels — a mentor, institution, or tradition whose guidance still deserves following, at least for now.
5.reversed: a rule kept out of pure habit, or a convention that stopped earning its loyalty a while ago.
5.advice: Learn the established path first. Decide whether to leave it after.

6.name: The Lovers
6.upright: a real alignment between people, values, or paths — a choice that matters because it says what you stand for, not just what you like.
6.reversed: a mismatch quietly put up with, or a decision dodged because naming it out loud would open a harder conversation.
6.advice: Name the choice plainly, even if the honest answer makes things messier.

7.name: The Chariot
7.upright: forward motion won by holding two opposing forces in one hand and steering them both the same way.
7.reversed: momentum eaten up by internal conflict, or a victory chased so hard it tramples the very thing it was supposed to protect.
7.advice: Stop wrestling with your own contradictions. Point them the same way and go.

8.name: Strength
8.upright: power that never needs to raise its voice — a steadiness that comes from making peace with the hard thing, not burying it.
8.reversed: self-doubt wearing humility as a disguise, or force reached for where patience would have done more.
8.advice: Meet what frightens you with calm instead of force. Gentleness isn't weakness.

9.name: The Hermit
9.upright: a necessary retreat — stepping back from the noise to hear what you think, not just what everyone around you is saying.
9.reversed: isolation curdling into avoidance, or wisdom held so close it never reaches the people who need it.
9.advice: Take the solitude. Whatever answer you're after won't turn up in a crowd.

10.name: Wheel of Fortune
10.upright: a shift already underway, pushed by forces bigger than any single choice — circumstance turning in a way that changes the terms of things.
10.reversed: a cycle repeating itself because the pattern underneath hasn't changed — only its costume has.
10.advice: Stop trying to control the turning. Put your energy into how you respond once it lands.

11.name: Justice
11.upright: a fair reckoning, even if not a comfortable one — clear eyes on cause and effect, and on what's owed.
11.reversed: an imbalance nobody's addressed, or a truth being sidestepped because facing it head-on would demand accountability.
11.advice: Look at the situation without flattering yourself. Fairness begins with an honest accounting.

12.name: The Hanged Man
12.upright: progress made by pausing instead of pushing — a deliberate suspension that opens up an angle on things you couldn't reach while moving.
12.reversed: delay for its own sake, or a sacrifice that never earned any real understanding in return.
12.advice: Let this stay unresolved a while longer. The insight lives inside the waiting, not somewhere past it.

13.name: Death
13.upright: a true ending that clears room for something that couldn't have existed alongside it — not destruction, but necessary change.
13.reversed: a change resisted long after it became inevitable, which only makes the ending harder once it does arrive.
13.advice: Let the part of this that's already over be over. Something else needs the space it's taking up.

14.name: Temperance
14.upright: two things that looked incompatible settling into a workable middle — patience, blending, the slow craft of getting the proportions right.
14.reversed: too much in one direction, or a compromise thrown together so fast neither side ends up satisfied.
14.advice: Slow the mixture down. The right balance won't be forced into place overnight.

15.name: The Devil
15.upright: a pattern, habit, or dynamic with more grip on you than you'd like to admit — even though the door out was never locked.
15.reversed: the first real pull away from something that had you trapped — seeing the chain clearly for what it is.
15.advice: Look honestly at what you keep choosing even though it costs you. Naming it is where the way out starts.

16.name: The Tower
16.upright: a structure built on shaky ground, coming down fast — disruptive, but clarifying, since it clears out what was never stable to begin with.
16.reversed: a collapse held off through sheer avoidance, or a smaller disruption that still shakes something loose.
16.advice: Don't rush to rebuild exactly what fell. Ask first why it couldn't stand.

17.name: The Star
17.upright: quiet hope returning after a hard stretch — not naive optimism, but a real sense that things can be mended and are heading somewhere better.
17.reversed: hope wearing thin, or an upbeat outlook that's drifted loose from any actual plan.
17.advice: Let yourself hope again. You've earned it, and it's pointing somewhere real.

18.name: The Moon
18.upright: a situation lit by something other than plain fact — instinct, imagination, and old fears mixing together, so what you're seeing isn't the whole picture yet.
18.reversed: confusion beginning to lift, or a fear that turns out to have loomed bigger in imagination than in reality.
18.advice: Don't force a decision while the picture's still this unclear. Wait for more light.

19.name: The Sun
19.upright: plain good fortune — clarity, warmth, a result that doesn't need a second guess.
19.reversed: joy dimmed by overthinking it, or a success that isn't being allowed in and enjoyed for what it is.
19.advice: Let this be as good as it is. You don't need to go looking for the catch.

20.name: Judgement
20.upright: an honest reckoning with where you've been, and a call to step into a version of yourself that matches what you've learned.
20.reversed: self-judgment curdling into harshness, or a wake-up call getting put off a little longer.
20.advice: Answer the call plainly. Whatever you've been avoiding is ready to be faced now.

21.name: The World
21.upright: a cycle closing cleanly, everything it was meant to teach already in hand — a real sense of arrival before the next journey starts.
21.reversed: a near-completion still missing its last piece, or closure being reached for before it's time.
21.advice: Acknowledge how far this has come before rushing toward whatever's next.

ace.upright: a burst of creative energy arriving all at once — an idea, offer, or venture that hasn't been shaped yet but is already pulling you toward it.
ace.reversed: inspiration that keeps stalling before it becomes action, or excitement for a new venture that's cooling off before it even starts.
ace.advice: Act on the spark now, while it's still hot. Waiting for the perfect plan will only let it fade.

two.upright: standing at a comfortable vantage point with real options ahead, weighing what you've already built against where you could take it next.
two.reversed: playing it too safe out of fear of the unknown, or a plan for the future that never gets put to the test.
two.advice: Stop admiring the view from where you're standing. Pick a direction and start walking toward it.

three.upright: the wait after the work is done — ships already sent out, results not yet in, but the groundwork solid enough to trust.
three.reversed: delays piling up on a plan that looked sure to work, or a widened view that's revealing obstacles you hadn't planned for.
three.advice: Keep your eyes on the horizon a little longer. What you set in motion is still on its way.

four.upright: a milestone worth stopping for — a homecoming, a celebration, a sense of having earned this particular moment of ease.
four.reversed: a celebration that feels hollow, or a sense of home and belonging that hasn't quite been reached yet.
four.advice: Let yourself enjoy this fully. Not every good moment needs to be immediately followed by the next task.

five.upright: competing wills clashing in the open — noisy, maybe exhausting, but honest, and better than the same tension left to simmer underground.
five.reversed: conflict losing steam at last, or a rivalry that turns out to have been more posturing than substance.
five.advice: Don't mistake this friction for failure. Competing ideas sharpen each other when no one's afraid to disagree out loud.

six.upright: a win that others can see too — recognition arriving publicly for effort that was, until now, mostly invisible.
six.reversed: pride curdling into arrogance, or a victory that never got the recognition it deserved.
six.advice: Accept the recognition without over-explaining it away. You earned the win; let it stand.

seven.upright: holding a position everyone else is now trying to take from you — tiring, but proof that what you built is worth defending.
seven.reversed: giving up ground you didn't need to, or defending a position so long you've lost sight of why it mattered.
seven.advice: Hold your ground, but check that you're still fighting for the right hill.

eight.upright: everything suddenly moving at once — messages landing, plans accelerating, a stretch of rapid motion after a long wait.
eight.reversed: momentum stalling right when it mattered most, or things moving so fast that nothing has time to land.
eight.advice: Move quickly while the path is clear, but don't outrun your own ability to respond to what comes next.

nine.upright: one more effort asked of you after a long series of them — tired, wary, but still standing, and closer to the end than it feels.
nine.reversed: defensiveness that's hardened into isolation, or exhaustion that's making every remaining challenge feel bigger than it is.
nine.advice: You've survived every round so far. Don't let guardedness stop you from accepting help with this last one.

ten.upright: carrying more than your share because you're close enough to the finish line that putting it down now feels wasteful.
ten.reversed: a burden kept out of stubbornness, or work set down at last after being carried for far too long.
ten.advice: Ask what you're carrying that was never yours to finish. Some of this weight can be shared or dropped.

page.upright: an idea too exciting to sit still with — restless curiosity that wants to test itself against the world immediately.
page.reversed: excitement with no follow-through, or plans announced loudly and then quietly abandoned.
page.advice: Let the enthusiasm move you, but give the idea at least one real test before chasing the next one.

knight.upright: charging toward the next thing with total confidence, driven more by appetite for the chase than by a fixed plan.
knight.reversed: recklessness that's starting to cost you, or restless energy with nowhere productive left to go.
knight.advice: Bring some of that boldness under control before it runs you, instead of you running it.

queen.upright: a warm, unshakeable self-assurance that draws people in without needing to perform for them.
queen.reversed: confidence that's turned brittle or demanding, or independence used to shut others out rather than stand on your own.
queen.advice: Lead with the confidence you already have. You don't need to prove it to anyone else first.

king.upright: leadership that inspires by example — a bold vision paired with the follow-through to make it real.
king.reversed: high expectations that have become impossible to meet, or ambition pursued so ruthlessly it burns the people helping you.
king.advice: Lead the vision, but check that the people carrying it out with you still want to be there.

ace.upright: an emotional cup filling past its rim — new love, new compassion, or a feeling so full it has to spill into something.
ace.reversed: an emotional opening that's being held back, or love and connection offered but not yet let in.
ace.advice: Let this feeling be as full as it is. There's no need to ration something this real.

two.upright: two people meeting each other as equals — a bond forming, or deepening, on mutual and roughly even terms.
two.reversed: a connection that's grown lopsided, or a partnership under a strain that hasn't been named out loud yet.
two.advice: Check that this connection is still as mutual as it started out. Say plainly what's shifted, if anything has.

three.upright: joy that's better shared — a gathering, a friendship, a moment worth celebrating with the people who've stood by you.
three.reversed: a group dynamic curdling into gossip or exclusion, or overindulgence dulling what should have been a real celebration.
three.advice: Bring the people who matter most into this moment. Celebration means more when it isn't done alone.

four.upright: boredom with what's already on the table, even though something worth noticing is being offered right in front of you.
four.reversed: apathy loosening its grip at last, or a willingness to look up and weigh the opportunity you'd been ignoring.
four.advice: Look up from what's disappointing you and notice what's being offered. It may be worth more than it first seemed.

five.upright: grief centered on what's spilled and gone, even while something intact is still standing close by, unnoticed.
five.reversed: grief starting to loosen its grip, or the first real steps toward accepting a loss rather than replaying it.
five.advice: Mourn what's truly gone, but turn around long enough to see what's still standing behind you.

six.upright: a pull back toward simpler times — old memories, familiar comforts, or a reunion with someone from an earlier chapter.
six.reversed: nostalgia that's become a hiding place, or an idealized past that's making the present look worse than it is.
six.advice: Visit the past for comfort, but don't move back in. What you need now lives in the present.

seven.upright: too many appealing options, some more solid than others, making it hard to tell real opportunity from wishful thinking.
seven.reversed: the fog clearing enough to see which options were ever real, and a decision becoming possible at last.
seven.advice: Test each option against reality before choosing. Not everything glittering here will hold up.

eight.upright: walking away from something that looks fine from the outside because it's stopped feeding you on the inside.
eight.reversed: staying somewhere out of fear of what leaving would mean, or drifting without ever fully committing to the departure.
eight.advice: Trust the part of you that knows this isn't enough anymore, even if you can't fully explain why yet.

nine.upright: an easy, comfortable satisfaction — a wish met, a want fulfilled, contentment that doesn't need to be justified.
nine.reversed: smugness standing in for real satisfaction, or abundance that somehow still doesn't feel like enough.
nine.advice: Let this contentment be simple. You don't need to earn it twice by worrying it won't last.

ten.upright: a deep, settled happiness built with the people closest to you — not a peak moment, but a lasting state.
ten.reversed: harmony at home that's more appearance than substance, or values among the people you love that have quietly stopped aligning.
ten.advice: Look past the surface picture of happiness and check that the people in it feel it too.

page.upright: a gentle, unexpected emotional or creative message arriving — something worth paying attention to, even if it seems small.
page.reversed: emotional immaturity getting in the way of a real opportunity, or a creative impulse used to escape rather than express.
page.advice: Take the small, unexpected feeling seriously. It's more informative than it looks.

knight.upright: leading with the heart, chasing a romantic or idealistic vision with real sincerity, even if it isn't fully practical yet.
knight.reversed: moodiness dressed up as sensitivity, or a romantic ideal that keeps setting you up for disappointment.
knight.advice: Follow your heart here, but check it against reality before you follow it all the way.

queen.upright: emotional depth held with real stability — compassion for others that doesn't come at the cost of your own footing.
queen.reversed: compassion that's tipped into self-neglect, or emotional security that only holds up as long as no one tests it.
queen.advice: Give others your compassion, but keep enough of it in reserve for yourself.

king.upright: a calm mastery over strong feeling — able to stay steady and fair even when the emotional stakes are high.
king.reversed: control over feeling that's really suppression, or calm on the surface hiding manipulation underneath.
king.advice: Stay steady, but let what you really feel be known rather than only managed.

ace.upright: a sudden cut through confusion — a realization, decision, or piece of truth arriving sharp and unmistakably clear.
ace.reversed: clarity that's been clouded by too much noise, or a truth that's been twisted before it reached you.
ace.advice: Trust the clear thought when it comes. Don't let it get talked back into confusion.

two.upright: a decision held at arm's length, guarded and balanced so carefully that neither option ever gets chosen.
two.reversed: the standoff breaking at last, or an overload of conflicting information making the choice harder rather than easier.
two.advice: Take the blindfold off. The decision won't get easier by delaying it further.

three.upright: a pain that's sharp and specific — a truth, betrayal, or loss that cuts precisely because it's real.
three.reversed: the first stages of healing, or old pain resurfacing because it was never fully dealt with the first time.
three.advice: Let the pain be exactly as sharp as it is. Naming it clearly is what starts the healing.

four.upright: a deliberate retreat after conflict or strain — not defeat, but the recovery a mind needs before it can think clearly again.
four.reversed: rest interrupted before it's finished, or restlessness that's making real recovery impossible.
four.advice: Take the rest fully. Half a recovery just means carrying the exhaustion into whatever comes next.

five.upright: a win that costs more than it's worth — a conflict pushed to the end even though everyone involved leaves worse off.
five.reversed: resentment lingering after a conflict that was never really resolved, or a chance to make peace instead of pressing the advantage.
five.advice: Ask whether winning this particular fight is worth what it will cost you afterward.

six.upright: a slow, deliberate move away from turbulence, carrying only what's necessary toward something steadier.
six.reversed: resisting a transition that's already necessary, or unresolved baggage being carried into the calmer waters ahead.
six.advice: Let the difficult waters be behind you. Don't keep looking back at the shore you're leaving.

seven.upright: moving quietly and independently, taking what you need without asking permission — clever, but not fully honest.
seven.reversed: a hidden strategy coming to light, or a guilty conscience catching up at last to a shortcut that was taken.
seven.advice: Ask whether the strategy you're running would still make sense if everyone involved could see it.

eight.upright: feeling boxed in on every side, even though the ropes holding you are looser than they feel — a prison built more from belief than from fact.
eight.reversed: the first real crack in that self-imposed trap, as the story of being powerless starts to loosen its grip.
eight.advice: Look for the gap in the ropes you've been assuming were solid. There's more room to move than it feels like.

nine.upright: a mind running worst-case scenarios in the dark, exhausted by fears that loom far larger at 3am than in daylight.
nine.reversed: worry starting to ease, or a decision to speak the fear aloud at last instead of carrying it alone.
nine.advice: Say the worry out loud to someone. It rarely survives contact with daylight as intact as it feels right now.

ten.upright: an ending that's as final as it is painful — the worst of it already behind you, with nowhere to go from here but up.
ten.reversed: resisting an ending that's already happened, or a slow, partial recovery from something that hasn't fully healed yet.
ten.advice: Let this ending be complete. Fighting to keep it half-alive only prolongs the pain of it.

page.upright: an alert, questioning mind, gathering information and watching closely before deciding what to believe.
page.reversed: gossip standing in for real investigation, or ideas that never move past talk into actual action.
page.advice: Keep asking questions, but eventually act on what the answers tell you.

knight.upright: moving fast and speaking plainly, cutting straight to the point without waiting for anyone's permission.
knight.reversed: aggression outrunning judgment, or impulsive decisions made faster than the situation required.
knight.advice: Act decisively, but take one breath before you speak the sharpest version of what you're thinking.

queen.upright: seeing situations plainly and saying so without softening it more than the truth requires.
queen.reversed: directness that's tipped into coldness, or boundaries held so rigidly that no one can get close.
queen.advice: Keep the clarity, but check whether the bluntness is necessary or just easier than being gentle.

king.upright: judgment made on principle and evidence rather than feeling — fair, precise, and hard to argue with.
king.reversed: logic used as a weapon, or authority that's technically correct while still being cruel.
king.advice: Be right, but don't let being right excuse being unkind about it.

ace.upright: a concrete opportunity landing in your hands — practical, real, and worth building on rather than just admiring.
ace.reversed: an opportunity missed through poor timing or poor planning, or a promising start that never got followed through.
ace.advice: Take the practical step now. This kind of opportunity rewards follow-through more than enthusiasm.

two.upright: keeping several demands moving at once, adjusting on the fly rather than dropping any of them.
two.reversed: one too many priorities added to the mix, with something now slipping that shouldn't have.
two.advice: Look honestly at what you're juggling. Something here may need to be set down, not balanced harder.

three.upright: different skills combining into something none of them could build alone — solid progress made through real collaboration.
three.reversed: working in isolation on something that needed other hands, or a team that's stopped pulling in the same direction.
three.advice: Bring in the help this requires. This isn't a project built well alone.

four.upright: a tight grip on what you've built, prioritizing security over risk, even at the cost of some flexibility.
four.reversed: holding on so tightly that nothing new can get in, or fear of loss driving decisions more than any real threat.
four.advice: Loosen the grip slightly. What you're protecting isn't as fragile as it feels.

five.upright: real hardship, felt as much in isolation as in the loss itself — struggling while feeling like help is out of reach.
five.reversed: the first signs of support becoming available, or hardship starting to ease at last after a hard stretch.
five.advice: Look for the door that's open nearby. Help exists here, even if it doesn't feel like it yet.

six.upright: resources moving fairly between people — help given because it's needed, and received without shame.
six.reversed: generosity that comes with strings attached, or an exchange that's quietly become one-sided.
six.advice: Check whether what's being given here is free, or whether something's owed in return.

seven.upright: a pause to take stock of effort already invested, weighing whether it's paying off or needs to change course.
seven.reversed: impatience with a return that hasn't come yet, or effort continuing on a path that's stopped paying off.
seven.advice: Take the honest audit. Some of this effort deserves more patience; some of it deserves a new plan.

eight.upright: steady, repeated effort aimed at getting truly good at something — unglamorous, but exactly what mastery requires.
eight.reversed: perfectionism stalling real progress, or shortcuts being taken on work that deserved the full effort.
eight.advice: Keep doing the unglamorous repetitions. This is what skill looks like while it's being built.

nine.upright: comfort and abundance earned largely on your own — a self-sufficiency that doesn't need anyone's approval.
nine.reversed: success that looks good from the outside while feeling hollow, or overwork that's crowded out anyone to enjoy it with.
nine.advice: Enjoy what you've built without needing anyone else to confirm it counts.

ten.upright: stability that outlasts any one person — a legacy or foundation built to support more than just yourself.
ten.reversed: a legacy under strain, or family disagreements over resources threatening something built to last.
ten.advice: Protect what's meant to outlast you, but don't let disputes over it undo what it was built for.

page.upright: a practical opportunity worth studying closely — new, promising, and still in the stage of learning how it works.
page.reversed: unrealistic plans that haven't been tested against reality, or progress that's stalled before it really started.
page.advice: Study this opportunity closely before committing further. It's promising, but still unproven.

knight.upright: slow, methodical, reliable progress — no shortcuts, just consistent work that adds up over time.
knight.reversed: routine that's calcified into stagnation, or perfectionism so rigid it's stopped anything from shipping.
knight.advice: Trust the slow method that's working. It doesn't need to be faster to be effective.

queen.upright: practical care that shows up in tangible ways — comfort, resources, and groundedness offered generously to others.
queen.reversed: care for others coming at the cost of care for yourself, or insecurity about resources undermining that generosity.
queen.advice: Extend the same practical care to yourself that you so easily offer everyone else.

king.upright: material and financial mastery built over time, now generous enough to share the security it's created.
king.reversed: control over resources turning rigid or possessive, or financial security pursued at the cost of everything else.
king.advice: Use what you've built generously. Security that isn't shared eventually just becomes isolation.

faq.a: Shuffle the deck, then click any four cards from the open fan. Your four-card reading — Determinant, Past, Present, and Future — is revealed instantly. No birth date or personal number needed.
Yes, completely free, with no sign-up, no account, and no cost, ever.

faq.q: What does a reversed card mean?
faq.a: A reversed card (drawn upside down) points to blocked energy, a more internal version of the card's usual meaning, or something not yet fully expressed — read it together with the card's upright meaning, not as a simple opposite.

faq.q: Can I get more than one reading a day?
faq.a: Yes. Click "Do another reading?" after your results to shuffle a brand-new set of four cards any time — every draw is genuinely random.
